title: Company-wide policies and processes — access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard processes for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees, people-ops, finance, security, and engineering teams.

If you are unsure which sub-policy applies, start with the Access & Permissions and Data Management sections and follow the owner/team contacts listed.

1) Access & permissions

Purpose
- Ensure least-privilege access across systems while enabling teams to move quickly.
- Provide a clear request/approval flow and audit trail for access changes.

Scope
- Applies to cloud accounts, internal services (Console, CI/CD, monitoring), databases, vendor portals, and production systems.

Roles & ownership
- Access Owner (People Ops): manages joiners/leavers and company-wide role templates.
- System Owner (Service/product teams): approves role assignments for their service(s).
- Security (Security & Compliance): periodic audits and escalation on policy violations.

Standard roles and templates (examples)
| Role | Typical access | Owner team |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Developer | Non-prod infra, code repo, staging logs | Eng teams |
| SRE | Prod monitoring, runbooks, incident channels | Eng-SRE |
| Platform Admin | Console admin for dedicated infra | Eng-Platform |
| Finance | Billing portal, expense reports | Finance |

Access request flow (for any system)
1. Submit an access request via the Access Request form (Confluence link or /tools/access-request). Include: user email, requested role, justification, expiration date (max 90 days for temporary access).
2. System Owner approves or rejects within 3 business days.
3. People Ops provisions access and records request id in audit log.
4. Access is automatically expired on the provided expiration date.

Emergency access
- For urgent production debugging, request a temporary elevated access code via PagerDuty with a required post-incident review. Emergency grants must be documented within 24 hours.

Periodic review
- Quarterly entitlement reviews: Security triggers review tickets for all high-privilege roles. Owners must confirm or revoke within 10 business days.

2) Change management

Purpose
- Reduce risk to production systems and ensure traceability for configuration, infra, and schema changes.

Change categories
- Standard changes: low-risk, pre-approved (routine deployments, dependency updates).
- Minor changes: require change request and approval by service owner.
- Major changes: high-risk or cross-service changes requiring CAB review and scheduled maintenance window.

Process summary
1. File a Change Request (CR) in the Change Management system with: description, rollback plan, owner, impacted services, scheduled window, test plan, and monitoring checklist.
2. Service Owner/Manager approves for Minor changes. Major changes go to CAB (Change Advisory Board) with at least 72 hours notice.
3. Execute during approved window, run the monitoring checklist, and update CR with runbook and outcome.
4. Post-change review: within 3 business days capture metrics (latency, error-rate) and link to the CR.

Rollback requirements
- Every CR must include an automated rollback or manual rollback checklist with explicit verification steps (e.g., DB schema rollback SQL, traffic switch commands, cache invalidation steps).

Maintenance windows and blackout periods
- Weekly deployment window: Tue-Thu 02:00–06:00 UTC for non-critical changes.
- Blackout: major customer releases (announced) and company holiday periods; emergencies are handled via the incident process.

3) Data management

Purpose
- Protect customer and internal data integrity, ensure regulatory compliance (GDPR, CCPA where applicable), and define retention & access patterns.

Data classification (high level)
- Public: marketing materials, public docs.
- Internal: internal memos, runbooks.
- Confidential: customer non-PII configuration, internal financials.
- Restricted: customer PII, secrets, audit logs.

Storage & retention policy
| Data type | Storage location | Retention period | Owner |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Audit logs | Central logging (secure bucket) | 7 years | Security |
| PII (customer) | Encrypted DB | 5 years or per contract | Product/Legal |
| Development artifacts | Repo/artifact store | 1 year | Engineering |

Encryption & key management
- All Restricted data must be encrypted at rest and in transit. Keys are managed via our KMS provider and rotated annually. For Private deployments, customers must provide KMS integration details.

Data access approval
- Data access requests follow the Access & Permissions flow and must include business justification, query scope, and intended use. For any PII access, require documented DSR/contractual justification and Security approval.

Data deletion & incident handling
- Deletion requests are routed to Data Steward (Product) and Legal for customer-facing requests (DSRs). Incident containment follows the Incident Response Security playbook and must be reported to Security within 4 hours of discovery.

4) Procurement & expenses

Purpose
- Ensure accountable spend, timely vendor onboarding, and clear expense reimbursement practices.

Purchasing thresholds & approvals
| Amount (USD) | Approval required |
| ---: | --- |
| <$1,000 | Team lead |
| $1,000–$15,000 | Department manager + Finance |
| >$15,000 | VP-level + Finance + Legal review |

Procurement process (step-by-step)
1. Complete Purchase Requisition (PR) form with supplier, description, justification, and budget code.
2. Manager approves PR.
3. Finance validates budget and routes to Legal for contracts if >$15k or for SaaS with data access.
4. Procurement issues PO and records vendor in the Vendor Registry.

Expense submissions
- Submit expenses within 30 days using the Expense Portal. Attach receipts for all claims. Per-diem and travel guidelines are below. Finance will audit a sample of claims monthly.

5) Vendor management

Vendor onboarding checklist (minimum)
- Completed Vendor Profile entry (legal name, tax id, contact, AML/KYC where applicable).
- Security questionnaire: for vendors with data access, complete Security & Compliance vendor assessment.
- Contract signed and filed in contract repository.
- Vendor added to Vendor Registry and assigned an internal owner.

Vendor risk tiers & controls
- Tier 1 (High risk — has access to customer data/production): Contract + SOC2 or equivalent, annual security review, quarterly access attestations.
- Tier 2 (Medium risk — supports infrastructure but limited data access): Contract + security questionnaire, annual review.
- Tier 3 (Low risk — office supplies): Standard PO process.

Offboarding and termination
- Ensure revocation of accounts, retrieval/disposal of company assets, and confirmation of data deletion per contract. Legal and Security coordinate the data deletion verification for Tier 1 vendors.

6) Travel policies

Booking and approvals
- All travel must be pre-approved in the Travel Request form with estimated cost and business justification. Team lead approval required; trips >$5,000 require Director approval.

Allowed expenses and per-diem
- Economy class for flights under 6 hours; premium economy or business for flights >6 hours with Director approval.
- Hotel: mid-range business hotel (corporate rates preferred).
- Meals: per-diem cap $75/day domestic, $125/day international. Receipts required.

Safety & insurance
- Company travel insurance covers medical evacuation and emergency assistance. Employees must register travel to high-risk regions with People Ops.

Travel reimbursement flow
1. Submit completed Expense report with receipts within 30 days.
2. Manager verifies purpose and costs; Finance processes reimbursement within next payroll cycle.

7) Internal templates & examples

Access request template (use in Access Request form)
- Requestor: <name@redwood.com>
- System: <service-name>
- Role requested: <role>
- Justification: <business reason>
- Expiration date (ISO): YYYY-MM-DD

Change request (minimal fields)
- Change ID: <autogenerated>
- Owner: <team name>
- Type: Standard | Minor | Major
- Description: <summary>
- Rollback plan: <commands/steps>
- Monitoring checklist: <metrics/alerts>

Vendor security assessment checklist (snippet)
1. Does the vendor store customer data? Y/N
2. Data encryption at rest and in transit? Y/N
3. SOC2 or ISO attestation on file? Y/N (attach)
4. Data deletion obligations and proof of deletion process? (describe)

8) Governance, exceptions, and escalation

Exceptions
- Policy exceptions must be requested via the Exceptions Request form and include business justification, compensating controls, owner, and an expiration (max 90 days). Security & Legal approve exceptions.

Escalation path
- Operational questions: contact the Service Owner.
- Policy disputes or security concerns: Security@redwood.com.
- Procurement/contract issues: procurement@redwood.com.

9) Audit and compliance cadence
- Quarterly internal audits carried out by Security and Finance.
- Annual external audits (SOC2/ISO) coordinated by Security & Legal.
- Retention/reporting: audit logs retained per Data Management table.
